messages:
maria: heads up — seeing a correlated spike in GPU attach failures in us-west3 over the last 20m. IOPS on local NVMe shot up and some nodes hit write queue stall, causing k8s to fail GPU mounts. logs below. /cc @sean @josh :sadpanda:

sean: Yikes. Any recent changes to the cleaner/scrub schedule?

maria: night-cleaner finished a big backlog at 03:00, but this looks like a second wave. sample dmesg excerpt:
`[1734567.890] nvme0: write_queue_depth=512 -> 64, write timeout increased`
`[1734570.123] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 125872`

josh: can reproduce on a repro node — qdepth spikes then overlayfs fsyncs pile up. appears tied to ephemeral janitor concurrency. current config set to 16 concurrent sweeps.

lisa: @maria can you paste top output for iostat? would like to see r/s w/s latency distribution.

maria: pasted quick iostat: 
`Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s  r/s  w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util`
`nvme0n1: 0.00  3.00 12.00 560.00  48.00 20480.00  37.32  8.21  15.7  2.1  16.5  0.20 98.7`

ben: 98.7% util is nasty — that's saturating drive. We should avoid scaling GPU pods onto those nodes until it cools down. Is there a label we can use to cordon?

josh: yes, we can taint temporarily: `kubectl taint nodes <node> nvme-saturated=true:NoSchedule` — but we need an automated way to block the provisioning pipeline for ~10m windows or it will just try other nodes and hit same issue.

ops-bot: alert: GPU attach failures spike -> 42 events in last 15m for us-west3. Autoscaler suspended for group gpu-pool-usw3 for 2m by ops-bot (reason: attach-failure flood).

sean: good. mitigation plan: 1) throttle janitor concurrency from 16 -> 4; 2) add short-lived taint on hottest nodes; 3) temporarily route GPU provisioning to us-west1 until us-west3 stabilizes. Thoughts?

lisa: agree. also want to enable KV cache hotprefix drop for model-fine-tune routes to reduce write amplification during attach bursts. small config change on runtime side.

maria: implementing janitor throttle now. applying patch: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=4
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner
```

josh: I'll push a quick operator rule to taint nodes with avgqu-sz > 4 for 6m: `devops-runner` will deploy.

devops-runner: deploying rule: `node-metric-taint` v1.0 -> targeting nvme_avgq > 4, taint TTL 6m. will monitor for false positives.

ben: also suggest we raise preemptible fallback threshold so autoscaler doesn't immediately replace failed attachments with more preemptibles in same rack. Otherwise we just churn.

sean: good call. I'll open a quick config override on the autoscaler to prefer other regions for 30m.

maria: after throttle, iostat shows write queue depth dropped and %util declined to ~72% on sampled nodes. attach failure rate down to 6 events in last 5m (was 42). progress.

lisa: follow-up ask: can we add a nightly rate limiter so backlog drains slower to avoid these secondary waves? maybe exponential decay based on avgqu-sz. filing a ticket. :memo:

maria: created ticket INF-7842 with samples, logs, and mitigation steps. leaving autoscaler override for 30m, janitor concurrency set to 4 until further notice. thanks team :thumbsup:

josh: later — we should also add a probe on nvme SMART temp and throttling counters to alert earlier (pre-queue-saturation). small enhancement but could prevent next one.

ops-bot: resolved: autoscaler override lifted at 1748513200. monitoring window still open.

maria: closing thread if no regressions. will post postmortem if we see recurrence.
